issue_context.title: TimeZoneInfo StandardName, DisplayName changes
issue_context.body:
Steps to reproduce the issue
use Net Core 2.1 and Display StandardName and DisplayName on Windows os
use Net Core 3.1 and Display StandardName and DisplayName on Linux os

Expected behavior
We expect that the StandardNamas and DisplayNames to be the same from 2.1 to 3.1

Actual behavior
It seams that the behavior has changed from 2.1 to 3.1 on Linux os, the DisplayName is replaced by StandardName and vice versa.
comments: Can you give concrete examples? (Code and output before/after)
@cristina-dorotan I am closing this issue but feel free to respond back with any question or request and we'll be happy to assist you and reactivate if necessary.

@tarekgh @danmosemsft 
I opened the ticket because they are mixed up in Linux, NOT because StandardName is not equal with DisplayName.

I am saying that StandardName in Windows != StandardName in Linux and 

This happens after the upgrade, as I mentioned before we are using nosinovacao/dotnet-sonar:latest as build. 

I would expect them to be the same in different Operating Systems as they were before the upgrade.

Thanks @cristina-dorotan for the clarification. 

I am seeing some weird things. I have a full Ubuntu 18.04 VM and I am not able to repro the issue on it. But, on my WSL2 with Ubuntu 18.04, I am seeing the names are wrong. I'll look more into that to figure out what is wrong.

> @danmosemsft we'll try to have some nicer solution for this issue in 5.0 but the question is, do we need to service this in 3.1? we already have a simple workaround if needed.

3.1 is an LTS release. To service we need a combination of significant/widespread customer impact and acceptably low risk. This sounds like mainly a display issue and with a good workaround. So it does not seem a servicing candidate.
